successCriteria.description: A new describe block covering the APPROVED reversal path exists inside tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts (no second test file), and the full Jest suite passes green.

Immutability acceptance test: after cancelling an APPROVED request, the original row still reads status APPROVED with approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt unchanged, and the fake repository recorded ZERO update calls against the original id; a NEW row is created with status CANCELLED, reversesRequestId === original.id, requestedDays === 0, approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt/submittedAt all null, cancelledBy === actor.id, cancelledAt set, and employeeId/leaveTypeCode/startDate/endDate/reason copied from the original.

Single-release test: usedDays is decremented by exactly the ORIGINAL row's requestedDays (not the reversal's 0), pendingDays is untouched, the balance is read with forUpdate = true before the write, and exactly ONE balance update call is recorded (no double release, no skipped release).

Side-effects test: exactly one CANCEL audit entry (AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType 'leave_request', entityId === the ORIGINAL id) and exactly one cancellation notification to the requester are recorded.
Atomicity test: uow.callCount === 1 and the stub client is forwarded to the reversal insert, the balance read and write, the audit record and the notification create.
Terminality test: cancelling a row whose status is already CANCELLED throws ConflictError (409) and performs no insert, no balance write, no audit and no notification.
Regression: the existing DRAFT (no balance touch) and SUBMITTED (pendingDays release) cancel paths still pass unchanged, and the existing authorization, timing and NotFoundError guards still hold.
npm run build is clean, the full Jest suite is green, and npm run smoke is green.

constraints: Test-only phase: no production source changes. Do not modify src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts, leave.model.ts, leave.repository.ts, or any other src/ file.
Extend the existing suite at tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts only — do not create a second test file and do not rewrite the existing cancel describe block.
Reuse the existing eight in-memory fakes and the makeRequest/makeActor/makeBalance/makeEmployee/makePolicy fixtures; do not introduce parallel fakes or fixtures.
FakeLeaveRepository must record create calls together with the forwarded client and must implement findByReversesRequestId; makeRequest must carry reversesRequestId: null for originals.
Assertions must be containment-based (e.g. .some(...), length checks) rather than exact-call-order dependent, matching the existing suite's transaction assertions.
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks; use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS constraint no-any).
Tests must not query a database directly or import a pool/client; all data access goes through the injected fakes (GP-001).
Verification commands: build = tsc --noEmit; test = jest --passWithNoTests --forceExit; smoke = node scripts/smoke.js. All three must pass.
outOfScope: Any production source change to the leave service, model, repository, or other src/ modules — this phase is test-only.
Integration/e2e tests exercising the real PostgreSQL reversal path, the unique index on reverses_request_id, or the HTTP layer.
Rewriting or re-asserting the existing cancel describe block's DRAFT/SUBMITTED/authorization/timing cases beyond confirming they still pass.
Reconciling the stale reconciled.json text (audit entityId, findByReversesRequestId rationale) — documentation drift is not fixed in this phase.
New behavior for reversal rows (e.g. re-cancelling a reversal, listing reversals) beyond the terminality guard already implemented.

entityInvariants.invariant: Once APPROVED, the row is immutable with respect to cancellation: status stays APPROVED and approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt are never written. Cancellation of an APPROVED request must not produce any update against the original id.

A reversal row is a NEW row with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId pointing at the original id; it is terminal (never cancelled or reversed again) and carries requestedDays 0 so it reserves and releases nothing. Its employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate and reason mirror the original; approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt and decidedAt are null; cancelledBy is the acting actor and cancelledAt is set.

Cancelling an APPROVED request releases usedDays exactly once, by the ORIGINAL row's requestedDays; pendingDays is untouched. The balance row is read with forUpdate = true before the write, and exactly one balance update occurs.
Exactly one CANCEL audit entry is written per APPROVED cancellation, with entityType 'leave_request' and entityId equal to the ORIGINAL request id (not the reversal row id).
Exactly one cancellation notification is emitted to the requester (recipientId = original employeeId), related to the ORIGINAL request id.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Only the requester's direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request; the owner and non-direct managers are rejected with ForbiddenError. Missing/invalid actor is rejected with UnauthorizedError/ForbiddenError.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: A request already in status CANCELLED throws ConflictError (409) before any transaction work — no insert, no balance write, no audit, no notification. A leave whose startDate is today or earlier throws ConflictError. An unknown request throws NotFoundError.
The reversal insert must be invoked with the transaction client forwarded as the optional last parameter; the fake must record the forwarded client so the test can assert it equals the stub client.

Must exist on the fake and return the row whose reversesRequestId matches, or null. The service does not call it in the APPROVED path (terminality is a pre-transaction status guard), but the interface must remain implemented.
The APPROVED cancellation must read the balance with forUpdate = true before writing it; the fake records forUpdate so the test can assert it.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the existing eight in-memory fakes (FakeLeaveRepository, FakeBalanceRepository, FakeAuditService, FakeNotificationService, FakeValidationService, FakeEmployeeService, FakePolicyService, FakeUnitOfWork) and the makeRequest/makeActor/makeBalance/makeEmployee/makePolicy fixtures exactly as defined; do not duplicate them.

The reversal field names and semantics asserted must match the LeaveRequest contract: status, reversesRequestId, requestedDays, approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt, decidedAt, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate, reason.
The findByReversesRequestId signature (reversesRequestId: string, client?: PoolClient) and the create(input, client?) signature the fake implements must match the repository interface.

The asserted APPROVED-cancel behavior (no original update, reversal row creation, usedDays release by original requestedDays, CANCEL audit with entityId = original id, single notification, pre-transaction CANCELLED guard throwing ConflictError) must match the implemented service.
Transaction assertions must follow the existing containment-based pattern (uow.callCount === 1, client === uow.stubClient forwarded to each participating call) rather than exact call ordering.

integrationPoints.why: The tests exercise the implemented reversal behavior; the service is the system under test and must not be modified.
The fake must satisfy this interface, including the optional-last-parameter client convention.
Field names and nullability asserted by the reversal tests come from this contract.
Atomicity assertions rely on the FakeUnitOfWork stub client and callCount.
Status and audit-action enums asserted in the new cases.
